project.name: kvcompression
project.description: KV Policy (KVP): a framework of lightweight per-head RL agents that learn to rank KV cache entries by predicted future utility, enabling adaptive eviction in LLMs without modifying the underlying model.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package initializer for the kvcompression library that sets up OmegaConf resolvers, loads environment variables via dotenv, and configures Hydra for distributed training entrypoints.

nodes.name: load_envs
nodes.summary: Loads environment variables from a .env file (or searches for one automatically) using python-dotenv.

nodes.name: format_resolver
nodes.summary: OmegaConf custom resolver that applies Python format_spec string formatting to interpolated config values.

nodes.name: activations_dataset.py
nodes.summary: Defines QKVDataset, a PyTorch Dataset that loads pre-saved safetensors files containing per-layer query, key, and value activations along with attention metadata for RL agent training.

nodes.name: QKVDataset
nodes.summary: PyTorch Dataset that discovers and loads QKV activation shards stored as safetensors files, supporting train/eval splits and returning per-item attention tensors with metadata.

nodes.name: pad_collate.py
nodes.summary: Provides a DataLoader collate function that pads variable-length QKV tensors along the sequence dimension and assembles a batch-level attention mask for use in distributed training.

nodes.name: pad_collate_fn
nodes.summary: Collates a list of per-sample dicts into a padded batch, computing padding masks for both the full sequence length and the prompt-only prefix length.

nodes.name: train_agent_sampler_distributed.py
nodes.summary: Main distributed RL training entrypoint for the KVP sampler agent: orchestrates multi-GPU setup, data loading, RLOO trainer construction, checkpointing, evaluation, and S3 upload via the RLOOTrainingRecipeDistributed class.

nodes.name: RLOOTrainingRecipeDistributed
nodes.summary: Encapsulates the full distributed RLOO training lifecycle: initializes distributed process groups, loads datasets and environments, sets up the agent model with optional EMA and DDP wrapping, drives the train-eval loop, saves checkpoints, plots results, and uploads artifacts.

nodes.name: launch_training
nodes.summary: Bootstraps a RLOOTrainingRecipeDistributed instance and sequentially calls setup, train, plot_results, evaluate_best_model, upload, and cleanup with error-safe distributed barrier teardown.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Hydra-decorated entry function that invokes launch_training with the resolved OmegaConf config and finalizes the metrics manager.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package initializer for the metrics subpackage that re-exports MetricsManager to make it accessible at the kvcompression.metrics namespace.

nodes.name: _metrics_manager.py
nodes.summary: Implements MetricsManager, a distributed-aware training metrics tracker that aggregates scalar values across ranks, logs to W&B, generates matplotlib plots, manages run/figures directories, and tracks the best checkpoint path.

nodes.name: MetricsManager
nodes.summary: Centralized training metrics tracker with distributed gather support, W&B integration, per-metric history storage, running-average computation, and matplotlib grid visualization; manages run directory naming and best-checkpoint path derivation.

nodes.name: infinite_distributed_sampler.py
nodes.summary: Provides InfiniteDistributedSampler, a DistributedSampler subclass that loops forever over the dataset without stopping at epoch boundaries and supports resumable state via state_dict/load_state_dict.

nodes.name: InfiniteDistributedSampler
nodes.summary: Extends PyTorch DistributedSampler to yield an infinite stream of shuffled indices by auto-incrementing the epoch on each exhaustion, with serializable epoch state for checkpoint-based resume.

nodes.name: training_checkpointer.py
nodes.summary: Implements TrainingCheckpointer and the ResumeInfo dataclass, providing full checkpoint lifecycle management: saving, loading, best-model tracking, old-checkpoint pruning, random-state serialization, and distributed rank-0 broadcast of checkpoint paths.

nodes.name: ResumeInfo
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding resume state extracted from a loaded checkpoint: success flag, step index, best metric value, W&B run id, metric history, and RNG states.

nodes.name: TrainingCheckpointer
nodes.summary: Manages the full checkpoint lifecycle for distributed RL training: discovers and loads existing checkpoints from local disk, serializes model/optimizer/scheduler/RNG state, enforces a keep-N policy, saves a separate best-model file, and broadcasts checkpoint paths across distributed ranks.

nodes.name: attention_utils.py
nodes.summary: Core attention utility library providing functions to materialize full attention weight matrices, generate causal attention masks, and expand KV caches for grouped-query attention (GQA) heads across the kvcompression framework.
nodes.languageNotes: All four functions are pure tensor operations with no class state; materialize_attention_weights handles causal masking, padding masks, and NaN cleanup in a single pass over 120+ lines.

nodes.name: materialize_attention_weights
nodes.summary: Computes explicit softmax attention weight matrices from query and key tensors, handling causal masking, padding masks, and variable-length sequences while zeroing out NaN rows that arise from fully-masked queries.

nodes.name: get_attention_mask
nodes.summary: Generates a lower-triangular causal attention mask tensor for a given batch size and sequence length pair, suitable for autoregressive decoding.

nodes.name: expand_kv_for_gqa
nodes.summary: Expands both key and value cache tensors from KV-head space to full query-head space for grouped-query attention by repeating each KV head across its associated query heads.

nodes.name: expand_k_for_gqa
nodes.summary: Expands only the key cache tensor from KV-head space to full query-head space for grouped-query attention, used when value expansion is not required.

nodes.name: compressor.py
nodes.summary: Implements the KVCompressor context manager and LayerHeadCompressionConfig dataclass, providing the primary user-facing API for configuring and applying per-layer/per-head KV cache compression strategies via monkey-patched attention hooks.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a context manager pattern (__enter__/__exit__) to scope monkey-patching lifetime; includes multi-level conflict validation for wildcard vs. specific layer/head configs.

nodes.name: LayerHeadCompressionConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing a compression configuration for a specific layer/head combination, with wildcard support and priority ordering via specificity scoring and __lt__ for sort-based resolution.

nodes.name: KVCompressor
nodes.summary: Context-manager class that installs per-head compression configs into a model's attention layers by monkey-patching MHA forward methods, validates config consistency on construction, and exposes compress_caches() for explicit cache eviction.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the kv_cache subpackage, re-exporting CompressibleKVCache and CompressionStrategy (and related classes) as the public surface of the module.

nodes.name: compressible_attention.py
nodes.summary: Contains the monkey-patched MHA forward pass and setup_cache functions that replace standard torchtune MultiHeadAttention behavior with a compressible variant that routes KV updates through CompressibleKVCache and applies per-head compression strategies.
nodes.languageNotes: monkey_patched_mha_forward handles both prefill and decode paths, uses torch.compile-compatible flex_attention for the actual attention computation, and dispatches to CompressibleKVCache.update and compress.

nodes.name: monkey_patched_setup_cache
nodes.summary: Replacement for MultiHeadAttention.setup_cache that instantiates a CompressibleKVCache with a per-head strategy mapping derived from the supplied layer/head configs.

nodes.name: _build_head_strategy_mapping
nodes.summary: Builds a head-index-to-CompressionStrategy mapping for a given layer by resolving matching LayerHeadCompressionConfig entries by specificity, falling back to DummyCompressionStrategy for unconfigured heads.

nodes.name: monkey_patched_mha_forward
nodes.summary: Full replacement forward pass for MultiHeadAttention that performs QKV projection, RoPE embedding, GQA expansion, CompressibleKVCache update, mask construction, and flex_attention computation in a single unified function.

nodes.name: compressible_kv_cache.py
nodes.summary: Defines CompressibleKVCache, a KVCache subclass that stores per-head compression strategy objects alongside K/V/Q tensors and implements compress() to selectively evict cache entries using strategy-derived boolean masks.
nodes.languageNotes: Extends torchtune KVCache; uses register_buffer for all tensors so they participate in device/dtype moves and checkpointing; compress() runs per-head strategy evaluation and scatters surviving entries.

nodes.name: CompressibleKVCache
nodes.summary: Extends the base KVCache with per-head CompressionStrategy support, providing update(), compress(), and get_k_v_and_mask_for_attention() to manage evictable KV entries during autoregressive generation.

nodes.name: compressible_mha_layer.py
nodes.summary: Defines CompressibleMultiHeadAttention, a thin wrapper around torchtune MultiHeadAttention that adds a reset_cache() method and is the target class whose forward/setup_cache methods are monkey-patched by the hooks layer.
nodes.languageNotes: The class itself has minimal logic; its instances become compressible at runtime through monkey-patching from compressible_attention.py and hooks/compressor.py.

nodes.name: CompressibleMultiHeadAttention
nodes.summary: MultiHeadAttention subclass that carries a CompressibleKVCache reference and exposes reset_cache() for clearing the KV state between sequences.

nodes.name: compression_strategy_protocol.py
nodes.summary: Defines the CompressionStrategy Protocol and its concrete implementations: DummyCompressionStrategy (keep all), RandomCompressionStrategy (random eviction), and PressCompressionStrategy (delegates to a BasePress scorer for importance-based eviction).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses typing.Protocol for structural subtyping; PressCompressionStrategy bridges the kvcompression framework to the kvpress BasePress interface by calling press() to obtain per-token scores and converting them to boolean keep masks.

nodes.name: CompressionStrategy
nodes.summary: Abstract Protocol defining the CompressionStrategy interface: a get_mask() method that returns a boolean keep-mask tensor given KV cache contents and a target budget.

nodes.name: DummyCompressionStrategy
nodes.summary: No-op compression strategy that always returns an all-ones mask, effectively disabling eviction for the assigned head.

nodes.name: PressCompressionStrategy
nodes.summary: Compression strategy that wraps a kvpress BasePress scorer, optionally materializing attention weights for attention-based presses, then converts the scorer's output indices into a boolean keep-mask.

nodes.name: constants.py
nodes.summary: Defines project-wide constants used across the kvcompression package, providing a single source of truth for shared literal values.

nodes.name: costs.py
nodes.summary: Implements the core KV cache eviction cost computation, measuring the attention loss incurred by evicting cache entries at various cache sizes via batched tensor operations.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses PyTorch named-tuple-style dataclass (NamedTuple) for CostResult with a `.to(device)` convenience method; the batched_compute_cost function applies dynamic programming over sorted rankings to compute AUC-normalized future-attention cost.

nodes.name: CostResult
nodes.summary: Named-tuple-style dataclass holding the output of batched_compute_cost: per-sample cost, cost-per-cache-size, and valid sequence lengths, with a `.to(device)` method for device transfer.

nodes.name: batched_compute_cost
nodes.summary: Computes the batched KV eviction cost for a set of rankings against ground-truth attention weights, returning AUC-normalized future-attention scores across all cache sizes.

nodes.name: kvsorting_env.py
nodes.summary: Defines KVSortingEnvironmentV2, the RL environment in which per-head agents learn to rank KV cache entries by iteratively selecting tokens to evict and receiving rewards based on oracle-computed attention cost.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements a gym-style step/reset API adapted for batched, multi-head KV ranking; supports both online stepping and offline chunked reward computation for RLOO training.

nodes.name: KVSortingEnvironmentV2
nodes.summary: RL environment managing KV cache ranking episodes: loads batches of keys/queries, orchestrates step-wise token selection, computes oracle-based rewards, and exposes a chunk-level reward API for RLOO policy optimization.

nodes.name: base_reward_strategy.py
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract RewardStrategy base class that all reward implementations must extend, specifying the compute_reward interface for deriving scalar rewards from oracle cost results.

nodes.name: RewardStrategy
nodes.summary: Abstract base class defining the compute_reward(cost_result) interface that concrete reward strategies implement to convert oracle cost output into RL reward signals.

nodes.name: basic_strategies.py
nodes.summary: Provides the FutureAttentionAucNormalizedReward concrete strategy that extracts the AUC-normalized future attention cost from oracle results as the RL reward signal.

nodes.name: FutureAttentionAucNormalizedReward
nodes.summary: Concrete RewardStrategy that returns the squeezed AUC-normalized future-attention cost from a CostResult as the agent reward.

nodes.name: oracle.py
nodes.summary: Implements the Oracle class that materializes full attention weights from keys/queries and computes ground-truth KV eviction costs, serving as the reward signal source for RL training.

nodes.name: Oracle
nodes.summary: Computes oracle KV eviction cost by materializing exact attention weights from raw keys and queries, then calling batched_compute_cost to score agent rankings against the ground truth.

nodes.name: utils.py
nodes.summary: General utility functions for the kvcompression package: model unwrapping, agent checkpoint loading, reproducibility seeding, torch-compile detection, and recursive batch-to-device transfer.

nodes.name: instantiate_agent_from_ckpt
nodes.summary: Loads an agent model from a checkpoint file by reconstructing it with OmegaConf/Hydra config instantiation and restoring its state dict, stripping any module prefix from keys.

nodes.name: seed_everything
nodes.summary: Sets random seeds across Python random, NumPy, and PyTorch (CPU and CUDA) for full reproducibility, falling back to a random seed when none is provided.

nodes.name: batch_to_device
nodes.summary: Recursively transfers all tensors in a nested dict batch to the specified device, used throughout the training and environment code to move data from CPU to GPU.

nodes.name: get_underlying_model
nodes.summary: Retrieves the underlying nn.Module, unwrapping DDP or DataParallel if necessary.

nodes.name: base_press.py
nodes.summary: Defines BasePress, the abstract base class for all KV cache eviction strategies, specifying the sort/forward interface that concrete press implementations must fulfill.

nodes.name: BasePress
nodes.summary: Abstract base class for KV cache compression presses; defines sort (must be implemented by subclasses), forward (applies eviction given a compression ratio), requires_attention_weights, and supports_gqa hooks.

nodes.name: random_press.py
nodes.summary: Implements RandomPress, a baseline KV cache eviction strategy that assigns random scores to cache entries for shuffled eviction order.

nodes.name: RandomPress
nodes.summary: Concrete BasePress subclass that implements sort by generating random scores and returning their argsort, serving as a random-baseline eviction policy.

nodes.name: sampler_agent_press.py
nodes.summary: Implements SamplerAgentPress, the primary RL-based KV cache eviction press that loads a per-head sampler agent from a checkpoint (local or S3) and uses it to score cache entries for eviction.

nodes.name: SamplerAgentPress
nodes.summary: Main press that instantiates a trained RL agent from a local or remote S3 checkpoint, applies sink-and-window masking, and produces per-head KV ranking scores; supports GQA and attention-weight-free operation.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package init for kvcompression.tools that re-exports AgentRegistry and assignment generator utilities for external consumers.

nodes.name: agent_registry.py
nodes.summary: Provides AgentRegistry, which discovers, validates, and resolves checkpoint paths for per-head RL agents stored in an S3 bucket under a structured group/sweep/layer/head hierarchy.

nodes.name: AgentRegistry
nodes.summary: Registry class that uses an S3 filesystem to list sweeps, discover agents by layer/head, resolve and validate checkpoint paths, and print a structured summary of discovered agents.

nodes.name: assignment_generator.py
nodes.summary: Provides generate_composites and write_composites_file utilities that build composite agent assignment configurations mapping each transformer layer/head to its best available checkpoint path.

nodes.name: generate_composites
nodes.summary: Queries AgentRegistry to discover trained agents for all specified layers and heads, resolves their checkpoint paths, and returns a sorted list of composite agent assignment dicts.

nodes.name: write_composites_file
nodes.summary: Wraps generate_composites and writes the resulting composite assignment list to a YAML file in the specified output directory.

nodes.name: s3_utils.py
nodes.summary: Provides S3/fsspec utilities for the kvcompression framework: filesystem construction, directory upload, file download, path mapping, remote secret loading, and remote folder listing.

nodes.name: get_s3_filesystem
nodes.summary: Constructs and returns an fsspec S3FileSystem configured from AWS environment variables including endpoint URL, credentials, and SSL verification settings.

nodes.name: upload_directory
nodes.summary: Recursively uploads a local directory to an S3 remote path using fsspec, with logging of transfer duration and error handling.

nodes.name: download_file
nodes.summary: Downloads a file or directory from an S3 remote path to a local destination using fsspec, with timing and error logging.

nodes.name: load_remote_json_secrets
nodes.summary: Downloads a JSON secrets file from S3 and sets its key-value pairs as environment variables, with distributed-training barrier synchronization between ranks.

nodes.name: ls_remote_folder
nodes.summary: Lists all files recursively under an S3 remote path using fsspec find, returning a sorted list of paths.

nodes.name: base_agent.py
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract BaseAgent class that all KV cache RL agents must implement, providing shared logic for action sampling, masked softmax selection, and entropy-based exploration.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses PyTorch Categorical distributions for stochastic action sampling with optional greedy argmax fallback.

nodes.name: BaseAgent
nodes.summary: Abstract base class for RL agents in the KV cache eviction framework, defining the interface for forward pass, action sampling with masked logits, and action mask creation.

nodes.name: kv_sorting_agent.py
nodes.summary: Implements KVSamplingGroupedQueryAgent, a neural network agent that scores KV cache entries for eviction by combining projected key, value, positional, and query-aggregated features through an MLP, supporting grouped-query attention (GQA).
nodes.languageNotes: Builds separate feature streams (key projection, value projection, positional embedding, key-difference cosine similarity, query aggregation) that are concatenated and passed through an MLP for final eviction scoring.

nodes.name: KVSamplingGroupedQueryAgent
nodes.summary: Concrete RL agent that produces per-token eviction scores for KV cache entries by projecting key/value tensors, computing positional and key-difference features, aggregating queries under GQA, and feeding combined features through a multi-layer MLP.

nodes.name: base_env.py
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract BaseEnvironment interface that all KV cache RL environments must implement, exposing reset, step, and get_valid_actions methods.

nodes.name: BaseEnvironment
nodes.summary: Abstract base class defining the standard RL environment interface (reset, step, get_valid_actions) for KV cache eviction environments.

nodes.name: compute_advantages.py
nodes.summary: Provides two utility functions for computing RLOO-style advantages from terminal rewards: a loop-based version and a vectorized version, both supporting optional advantage normalization.

nodes.name: compute_returns_and_advantage
nodes.summary: Computes per-step RLOO advantages for a batch of episodes using a loop over valid episodes, with optional mean/std normalization across the batch.

nodes.name: compute_returns_and_advantage_vec
nodes.summary: Vectorized version of advantage computation that uses tensor broadcasting to expand per-episode advantages across timesteps, more efficient than the loop-based variant.

nodes.name: rloo_gumbel_terminal_trainer.py
nodes.summary: Extends RLOOTerminalTrainer with a Gumbel-noise-based trajectory collection strategy that replaces stochastic categorical sampling with Gumbel-top-k sorted ordering, enabling differentiable or diverse rank-based eviction decisions.
nodes.languageNotes: Adds Gumbel noise (log(-log(u))) to agent scores before argsort, converting score ranking into a form of stochastic sorting without requiring categorical sampling.

nodes.name: RLOOGumbelTrainer
nodes.summary: Trainer subclass that overrides collect_trajectories and evaluate to use Gumbel-perturbed scores for producing sorted eviction orderings, while inheriting the RLOO policy update and metrics infrastructure from RLOOTerminalTrainer.

nodes.name: rloo_terminal_trainer.py
nodes.summary: Core RLOO (Reward-Linked Online Optimization) trainer that manages the full RL training loop for KV cache eviction agents, including trajectory collection with sequential token eviction, policy updates with entropy regularization, EMA model maintenance, and evaluation with plotting utilities.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements terminal-reward RL where each episode corresponds to evicting tokens from a KV cache sequence and the reward is only observed at episode termination; supports both sequential action-by-action eviction and precomputed-score bulk eviction modes.

nodes.name: RLOOTerminalTrainer
nodes.summary: Full-featured RLOO trainer orchestrating trajectory sampling from BaseEnvironment, advantage computation, policy gradient updates with entropy loss and gradient clipping, EMA-based evaluation agent, and per-metric logging and plotting across training and evaluation phases.

nodes.name: chunk_sampler.py
nodes.summary: Defines ChunkSampler, a PyTorch-compatible sampler that partitions a dataset into fixed-size sequential chunks and optionally shuffles indices within those chunks for reproducible batched data loading.

nodes.name: ChunkSampler
nodes.summary: A sampler that yields dataset indices in fixed-size chunks, with optional shuffling controlled by a random seed for reproducibility.

nodes.name: kvpress_dataset.py
nodes.summary: Wraps a Hugging Face dataset for KVPress preprocessing, providing tokenized chat message pairs with row-level IDs used during KV cache data generation.

nodes.name: KVPressPreprocessingDataset
nodes.summary: Dataset wrapper that loads a HuggingFace dataset, assigns row IDs, and tokenizes prompt/completion message pairs for use in KV cache generation pipelines.

nodes.name: unroll_and_store.py
nodes.summary: Entry-point script for KV cache data generation: runs forward passes on a language model while intercepting attention tensors via hooks, then saves the resulting Q/K/V tensors and generated tokens to disk (and optionally S3) for downstream RL training.

nodes.name: InferenceRecipe
nodes.summary: Orchestrates model loading, data setup, generation, and per-sample storage of attention tensors and tokens, using a thread pool for concurrent disk/S3 writes.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Top-level entry function that logs the config, instantiates InferenceRecipe, and runs setup then generation.

nodes.name: extractors.py
nodes.summary: Provides the ExtractAttentionTensors context manager that intercepts attention module forward calls to capture and persist per-layer, per-head Q/K/V tensors to disk during model inference.

nodes.name: ExtractAttentionTensors
nodes.summary: Context manager that registers forward hooks on attention modules to intercept Q/K/V tensors and save them as safetensors files organized by layer and head, handling both GQA and MHA layouts.
nodes.languageNotes: Handles both grouped-query attention (GQA) and multi-head attention (MHA) layouts by branching on the ratio of query heads to KV heads.

nodes.name: registrar.py
nodes.summary: Implements low-level hook registration utilities for attaching forward hooks and monkeypatching attention modules in a torchtune-style transformer, returning context managers that clean up hooks on exit.

nodes.name: register_attention_forward_hook
nodes.summary: Registers a post-forward hook on every attention layer of the model, wrapping callee invocations so the hook receives Q/K/V tensors; returns a context manager that removes hooks on exit.

nodes.name: monkeypatch_multihead_attention
nodes.summary: Replaces attention forward and setup_cache methods via monkeypatching to intercept calls with custom implementations, and registers a forward hook; returns a context manager restoring original methods.

nodes.name: test_generate_with_compression.py
nodes.summary: End-to-end tests for the generate_with_compression function, verifying that the compressed generation matches torchtune baseline output when no compression or noop compression is applied, differs when real compression is used, and raises errors on invalid batch sizes.

nodes.name: create_model
nodes.summary: Pytest fixture that constructs and returns a deterministically initialized test model on the appropriate device.

nodes.name: test_matches_torchtune_without_compression
nodes.summary: Verifies that generate_with_compression without a compressor produces token sequences identical to the vanilla torchtune generation path.

nodes.name: test_differs_from_torchtune_with_real_compression
nodes.summary: Asserts that applying a real (RandomCompressionStrategy) KVCompressor causes generate_with_compression to diverge from the baseline torchtune output.

nodes.name: test_matches_torchtune_with_noop_compression
nodes.summary: Confirms that a noop (DummyCompressionStrategy) compressor does not alter generation outputs relative to the torchtune baseline.

nodes.name: test_batch_size_validation
nodes.summary: Checks that generate_with_compression raises an error when called with a batch size other than 1.

nodes.name: test_compressor.py
nodes.summary: Comprehensive test suite for the KVCompressor component, covering forward-pass output equivalence with noop strategies, generation-level equivalence, and divergence verification when non-trivial compression strategies (RandomPress, PressCompressionStrategy) are applied.

nodes.name: TestKVCompressorEquivalence
nodes.summary: Test class grouping three methods that validate KVCompressor output equivalence properties: noop output equivalence, generation equivalence, and non-equivalence under real compression.

nodes.name: test_patched_model_forward.py
nodes.summary: Tests that a model patched with a KVCompressor using a noop compression strategy produces logits numerically close to those of the unpatched model during a forward pass.

nodes.name: test_patched_model_forward
nodes.summary: Runs an unpatched and a KVCompressor-patched model forward pass on the same inputs and asserts logit closeness using torch.allclose.

nodes.name: test_online_attention.py
nodes.summary: Test suite for online attention mechanisms, validating attention weight rematerialization equivalence, GQA (grouped-query attention) key/value expansion correctness, and edge cases for the materialize_attention_weights utility.

nodes.name: test_attention_rematerialization_equivalence
nodes.summary: Verifies that attention weights computed via materialize_attention_weights match those from scaled_dot_product_attention for various batch, sequence, and head configurations.

nodes.name: _setup_model_and_run_forward
nodes.summary: Helper that builds a deterministically initialized model with KVCompressor, runs a forward pass, and extracts KV cache contents and queries needed for attention rematerialization tests.

nodes.name: _verify_attention_outputs
nodes.summary: Asserts shape correctness, numerical closeness to SDPA output, and valid probability distribution of rematerialized attention weights.

nodes.name: test_gqa_expansion_correctness
nodes.summary: Tests that expand_kv_for_gqa correctly tiles key/value tensors from KV-head count to query-head count for grouped-query attention.

nodes.name: test_edge_cases
nodes.summary: Covers edge cases for materialize_attention_weights including single-token sequences and masked attention patterns.

nodes.name: test_utils.py
nodes.summary: Shared test utilities providing deterministic tensor and model initialization helpers (fixed_init_tensor, fixed_init_model) and a base_test_model factory used across the entire test suite to ensure reproducible test setups.

nodes.name: fixed_init_tensor
nodes.summary: Creates a tensor with a deterministic, reproducible pattern based on element indices, supporting optional nonlinear (sin) transforms and configurable value ranges.

nodes.name: fixed_init_model
nodes.summary: Initializes all parameters of a model in-place using fixed_init_tensor to ensure reproducible weight values for testing.

nodes.name: base_test_model
nodes.summary: Factory function that builds a Llama2-based test model via Llama2Builder, applies fixed initialization, and moves it to the specified device in eval mode.

nodes.name: .env.template
nodes.summary: Template for runtime environment variables covering data root path, HuggingFace model ID, S3 bucket, Weights & Biases settings, and optional torch.compile disable flag; intended to be copied to .env and sourced before running preprocessing, training, or inference scripts.

nodes.name: .pre-commit-config.yaml
nodes.summary: Pre-commit hook configuration enforcing trailing-whitespace removal, end-of-file fixing, YAML validity, merge-conflict detection, and Ruff-based linting and formatting on every commit.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Ruff (astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit v0.9.6) for both lint (--fix) and format passes, replacing older flake8/black combos.

nodes.name: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
nodes.summary: Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct (7 sections) defining community standards, maintainer responsibilities, scope of enforcement, and reporting procedures for unacceptable behavior.

nodes.name: CONTRIBUTING.md
nodes.summary: Brief contribution guide directing contributors to read CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md before getting started; serves as the entry point for new contributors.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Primary project documentation covering installation, dataset generation, training, and inference for the KVP (KV Policy) framework — lightweight per-head RL agents that learn to rank KV cache entries by predicted future utility for adaptive LLM eviction; includes citation, acknowledgements, and license sections.

nodes.name: pyproject.toml
nodes.summary: Python project manifest for the kvcompression package defining build system (setuptools + git-versioning), runtime dependencies (PyTorch, flash-attn, transformers, torchtune, wandb, s3fs, etc.), uv workspace source and dual PyTorch index configuration for CPU vs CUDA 12.8 platforms, and tool settings for pytest, mypy, and ruff.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses uv workspace with explicit PyTorch package indexes split by sys_platform to serve CPU wheels on non-Linux and CUDA 12.8 wheels on Linux; flash-attn requires special extra-build-dependencies workaround due to a known uv issue.

nodes.name: .understandignore
nodes.summary: Ignore rules for the understand-anything knowledge graph tool, listing paths and patterns that should be excluded from analysis (e.g., binary assets, generated files, large data splits).

nodes.name: ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS
nodes.summary: Credits and attribution notice listing third-party libraries, datasets, and prior work that the kvcompression project builds upon.

nodes.name: train.txt
nodes.summary: Training split index file for the RULER benchmark dataset, listing 6175 sample identifiers used to select KV cache training examples for RL agent learning.

nodes.name: val.txt
nodes.summary: Validation split index file for the RULER benchmark dataset, listing 325 sample identifiers used to evaluate RL agent performance during and after training.

nodes.name: preprocess_ruler.yaml
nodes.summary: Configuration for the RULER dataset preprocessing pipeline, specifying the model, tokenizer, data directories, chunking parameters, device settings, and KV cache generation options used to produce training data.

nodes.name: agent_training_setup.sh
nodes.summary: Shell setup script for initializing a single RL agent training job: installs system and Python dependencies via uv, then downloads only the specific layer/head KV cache data needed for training to /dev/shm for fast in-memory access.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses /dev/shm for RAM-backed storage to maximize I/O throughput during training data loading.

nodes.name: preprocessing_setup.sh
nodes.summary: Shell setup script for the KV cache preprocessing stage: validates the KVCOMPRESSION_MODEL_ID environment variable, installs dependencies via uv, and downloads the target LLM from HuggingFace using torchtune.

nodes.name: train_single_head.yaml

nodes.name: policy_entropy_loss.py
nodes.summary: Implements the REINFORCE policy gradient loss with entropy regularization for KV cache eviction agents; reconstructs valid action masks from episode history and computes policy and entropy losses over valid episode steps.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses masked Categorical distributions to correctly handle variable-length KV sequences and the progressive shrinking of the valid action set as entries are evicted.

nodes.name: compute_policy_entropy_loss
nodes.summary: Computes the REINFORCE policy gradient loss with entropy bonus by reconstructing per-step action masks from episode trajectories, applying masked Categorical distributions, and returning total, entropy, policy, and average entropy losses.

nodes.name: triton_policy_entropy_loss.py
nodes.summary: Implements a fused Triton GPU kernel for computing the combined policy gradient and entropy regularization loss in a single pass, including both forward and backward custom autograd functions for efficient RL training.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Triton JIT kernels (triton.jit) with tl (triton.language) intrinsics for massively parallel per-batch computation; the custom PyTorch autograd Function (PolicyEntropyLossTriton) manually implements both forward and backward passes, bypassing PyTorch's autograd graph for numerical precision and performance.

nodes.name: PolicyEntropyLossTriton
nodes.summary: Custom torch.autograd.Function that dispatches policy entropy loss computation to Triton GPU kernels, handling forward loss accumulation and backward gradient propagation through policy logits.

nodes.name: _policy_entropy_loss_forward_kernel
nodes.summary: Triton JIT kernel that computes per-step log probabilities and entropies from policy logits in the forward pass, writing results to flat output buffers for later loss aggregation.

nodes.name: _policy_entropy_loss_backward_kernel
nodes.summary: Triton JIT kernel that computes and accumulates gradients with respect to policy logits for the combined policy loss and entropy regularization term in the backward pass.

nodes.name: compute_policy_entropy_loss_triton
nodes.summary: Public entry point that validates inputs, prepares tensors on the correct device, and invokes PolicyEntropyLossTriton.apply to compute the differentiable policy entropy loss using Triton kernels.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README introduces KVP (KV Policy), a framework that trains one lightweight RL agent per attention head to learn which KV cache entries to evict during LLM inference. Reading this first establishes the three-phase pipeline — dataset generation, distributed RL training, and inference deployment — that structures every other file in the tour.

tour.title: Attention Math Foundations
tour.description: Before anything else can work, the project needs a reliable implementation of attention score computation. `attention_utils.py` provides scaled dot-product attention, causal masking, and GQA (Grouped Query Attention) head expansion — primitives that are consumed by both the reward oracle and the RL environment. Understanding these building blocks makes the reward signal in later steps immediately clear.
tour.languageLesson: GQA (Grouped Query Attention) allows multiple query heads to share a single key/value head. When computing eviction scores you must expand the shared KV heads back to the full query-head count before comparing attention weights — that expansion is what GQA utilities handle here.

tour.title: Data Generation Pipeline
tour.description: `unroll_and_store.py` is the first entrypoint you would run in practice: it loads a Qwen2.5-7B model, runs a forward pass over the RULER long-context benchmark, and captures the raw Q/K/V activations from every attention layer, writing them to S3 as safetensors files. This step produces the offline dataset that the RL training loop consumes, completely decoupling expensive LLM inference from policy optimization.
tour.languageLesson: PyTorch forward hooks (registered via `register_forward_hook`) let you intercept intermediate tensor outputs without modifying the model's source code. The hook receives the module, its inputs, and its outputs as arguments — a clean pattern for activation capture at scale.

tour.title: Hook System: Activation Extractors
tour.description: `extractors.py` defines the hook functions that actually capture Q/K/V tensors during the forward pass, while `registrar.py` wires those hooks onto the correct attention modules inside the LLM. Together they form the observation layer of the entire framework: without them there is no signal for the RL agents to act on, and no oracle reward to train against.

tour.title: Offline Activation Dataset
tour.description: Once activations are stored on S3, `activations_dataset.py` exposes them as a PyTorch Dataset (`QKVDataset`) that loads safetensors files on demand. `chunk_sampler.py` sits alongside it and draws fixed-size token windows from variable-length sequences, turning each window into one RL training episode. This pair is what `train_agent_sampler_distributed.py` passes to the DataLoader.
tour.languageLesson: Safetensors is a memory-safe alternative to PyTorch `.pt` files: it supports zero-copy memory mapping, making it efficient to load large activation tensors from disk without copying them into RAM first.

tour.title: The RL Agent: Policy Network
tour.description: `base_agent.py` defines the abstract interface that all eviction policies must implement, while `kv_sorting_agent.py` provides the concrete `KVSamplingGroupedQueryAgent`: a GRU-based recurrent network that reads KV cache features (key norms, position encodings, attention statistics) and outputs a ranking score for each token. One instance of this agent is trained independently per layer-head pair — 112 total for Qwen2.5-7B.
tour.languageLesson: A GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit) processes a sequence of token features one at a time, maintaining a hidden state that summarizes context seen so far. Here it is applied across KV cache positions so the agent's score for each token can depend on what came before it.

tour.title: Oracle Reward Signal
tour.description: The oracle uses the full attention matrix — unavailable at normal inference time but available in training — to compute the ideal future utility of each KV entry. `oracle.py` calls into `costs.py` to derive a reverse cumulative sum over future attention weights (the AUC of a token's predicted attendance in future decoding steps), then `basic_strategies.py` normalizes that score into a scalar reward the RLOO trainer can consume.

tour.title: RL Environment
tour.description: `base_env.py` sets the abstract contract for any RL environment in the project; `kvsorting_env.py` implements `KVSortingEnvironmentV2`, which frames KV cache eviction as a sequential decision problem. At each step the agent receives a chunk of Q/K/V features, selects a ranking over tokens, and receives the oracle AUC reward at episode termination. This environment is the bridge between the dataset, the policy network, and the trainer.

tour.title: RLOO Trainer
tour.description: `rloo_terminal_trainer.py` is the heart of the learning loop: it runs multiple rollouts per update, waits for the terminal (episode-end) reward, calls `compute_advantages.py` to compute RLOO baselines, then applies the REINFORCE policy-entropy loss from `policy_entropy_loss.py` to update the agent's weights. The Triton kernel in `triton_policy_entropy_loss.py` accelerates the loss computation on GPU for the scale of 112 parallel agents.
tour.languageLesson: RLOO (REINFORCE Leave-One-Out) reduces variance in policy gradient estimation: instead of subtracting a learned value baseline, each rollout's return is compared against the mean of all other rollouts in the same batch. This is computationally cheap and effective for small, parallel policies.

tour.title: Distributed Training Entrypoint
tour.description: `train_agent_sampler_distributed.py` orchestrates the full training run using PyTorch DDP: it instantiates one agent per head, wraps each in DistributedDataParallel, feeds batches from `QKVDataset` through `KVSortingEnvironmentV2`, and calls the RLOO trainer. It also manages checkpointing and W&B logging through the supporting utilities. `train_single_head.yaml` holds all the hyperparameters — RLOO group size, learning rate, KV budget ratio — that control a training run.
tour.languageLesson: PyTorch DDP (DistributedDataParallel) wraps a model and synchronizes gradients across all processes after each backward pass using an all-reduce collective. For 112 independent agents trained in parallel, DDP lets you split the per-head workload across multiple GPUs with minimal code change.

tour.title: Training Infrastructure
tour.description: Three supporting modules keep the training loop production-ready. `_metrics_manager.py` abstracts W&B and console logging behind a single interface. `training_checkpointer.py` saves and restores complete training state — model weights, optimizer state, and epoch counters — so runs can be resumed after preemption. `s3_utils.py` handles upload and download of checkpoints and datasets to S3, enabling fully cloud-based training pipelines.

tour.title: Press Abstraction & Compression Strategies
tour.description: `base_press.py` defines the `BasePress` interface that all eviction policies expose at inference time: given a KV cache and a target size, return the indices to keep. `compression_strategy_protocol.py` wraps that interface in a Protocol so it can be dependency-injected into the cache layer. `random_press.py` provides a random-eviction baseline — useful for establishing a lower bound on performance before evaluating trained agents.
tour.languageLesson: Python Protocols (from `typing`) define structural subtyping: any class that implements the required methods satisfies the protocol without explicitly inheriting from it. This is duck-typing made explicit and checkable by static analysis tools like mypy.

tour.title: KV Cache Engine
tour.description: `compressible_kv_cache.py` is a drop-in replacement for Hugging Face's default `DynamicCache` that intercepts each update step and applies a compression strategy when the cache exceeds a target token budget. `compressible_attention.py` and `compressible_mha_layer.py` patch the attention module itself so that every autoregressive decoding step passes through this eviction-aware cache, making compression fully transparent to the surrounding model.

tour.title: SamplerAgentPress: Trained Policy at Inference
tour.description: `sampler_agent_press.py` is where the trained RL agents re-enter the picture. `SamplerAgentPress` loads agent checkpoints via `AgentRegistry`, which discovers the per-head `.pt` files from S3 using the composite assignment YAML produced by `assignment_generator.py`. At inference time, for each attention head the press runs the corresponding agent forward to score the current KV entries, sorts by score, and evicts the lowest-ranked tokens to stay within the memory budget.

tour.title: End-to-End Inference Demo
tour.description: `generation.py` provides the high-level `generate()` function that wires together `CompressibleKVCache`, the hook registrar, and `SamplerAgentPress` into a single call, making it straightforward to run a compressed-inference generation loop with minimal boilerplate. The `inference_demo.ipynb` notebook then demonstrates this end-to-end: load the model, load the agents, generate text with a fixed KV budget, and compare output quality against full-cache generation.
